newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Thursday on short-covering but most investors were wary about the future market trend, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,530 yuan ($2,595) per tonne, rising 200 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 21,490 and hit a high of 21,640.
February rose 80 to 21,100, March 90 to 21,220, April 160 to 21,410, June 250 to 21,600 and July 120 to 21,600.
Combined volume fell to 34,480 tonnes from 93,370.
Copper opened higher and rose further before long liquidation pushing prices off their highs.
Traders said Shanghai copper opened higher due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but cautious market sentiment prevented it from rising further.
"Many long position holders, discouraged by Tuesday's poor performance on the LME, were eager to liquidate their positions at high levels," one trader said.
"Copper will have difficulty staying at high levels due to a lack of follow-up buying," he added.
Traders said copper was unlikely to fluctuate sharply with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"The holiday mood means few investors are building large positions, especially given the unclear short-term market trend," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move around 21,500 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended unchanged. The only traded February contract closed at 14,900 tonnes per tonne, unchanged from Wednesday's close, on volume of 170 tonnes.
